summary: China approves its first brainstem implant to help some deaf children hear, and tourists at 'China's Hollywood' pay to star in their own two-minute dramas.
body: China's medical products regulator approved the country's first auditory brainstem implant on Oct. 19, Sixth Tone reports [^1]. The device, the Nurotron WH-01A, is for deaf patients who cannot use an ordinary cochlear implant because their inner ear is badly malformed or the hearing nerve is missing. Instead of working through the ear, it stimulates a hearing centre in the brainstem directly [^1]. It was developed by surgeon Wu Hao's team at Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital with Zhejiang Nurotron Biotechnology, and trial patients included children aged 2 to 6 [^1][^2]. The developers report an effectiveness rate of almost 97% after a year of use; that figure is their own and has not been independently checked [^1]. A specialist blog notes the sound processing was designed for Mandarin's four tones [^2]. Brain-computer interfaces are one of six "future industries" in China's 2026-2030 five-year plan [^1].

In daily life, Hengdian World Studios in Zhejiang, China's largest film and TV base, now lets tourists star in a short drama of their own [^3]. Packages cost up to 388 yuan (about US$60) and include costumes, makeup and about an hour of filming; the finished two-minute drama arrives two days later [^3]. Nearly 3,000 people have tried it since July, choosing from scripts such as palace intrigue, martial-arts fantasy and "CEO romance" [^3]. Part of the reason is that real productions are fewer: cheaper AI-made dramas and platform cuts have reduced film shoots, Sixth Tone reports [^3]. My read: as AI changes how stories are made, places built for filming are turning into places where ordinary people get to perform.

reads.title: At China's Biggest Studio Complex, Tourists Pay to Play the Lead
reads.summary: A lively visit to Hengdian, where a farmer from Sichuan and a tourist from Peru pay to act in their own short dramas, and why the studios need them.
